Apple has updated the privacy policy of the Apple Store app, adding terms related to an upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Here are the details.

Apple is expanding its use of artificial intelligence in retail operations

According to MacRumors, the Apple Store App & Privacy page has added a new section called "Virtual Shopping Assistant", which reads as follows:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon feature a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses, helping users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says it will strip personally identifiable information from conversations before sharing them with unnamed partners that help provide the assistant's responses, which likely means some of the experience will be powered by third-party models from external companies.

Conversation history will be kept within the app for users to review at any time, and will also be retained by Apple for business analysis. Users can opt in to a new "Chat Improvements" setting, which allows their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant.

The wording of Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant will initially be available in select countries and regions, and may launch first in English-speaking markets before expanding to more languages and regions.

Months before this announcement, Apple had already added an AI-powered chatbot to its Sales Coach app, providing sales and technical resources for the company's retail partners. Accessible through the "Ask" tab, the chatbot draws on Apple's official training materials and documentation to answer questions.

Additionally, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" at select retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe, and summarise Genius Bar sessions, allowing staff to focus on helping customers without taking notes themselves.
